comparator.name: Economics and Governance (Bachelor Economie en Beleid)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: a 111-EC compulsory common part, a 3-EC restricted mathematics/statistics choice, one 24-EC thesis track and 42 EC of open electives. The Economics thesis track is selected by the official-order tie-break and is completed with the first two listed 6-EC restricted options plus the 12-EC thesis.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines microeconomics, macroeconomics, public economics, econometrics and behavioural economics with politics, law, sociology, inequality and institutions.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces accounting, marketing, business strategy, international business, product design, machine learning, probability and finance with comparative politics, sociology, qualitative methods, political philosophy, human rights, constitutional law, sustainability governance, EU politics, social theory, persuasive communication, peace and conflict, and historical research. The resulting curriculum is organised around institutions and policy rather than firms and business functions.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Economics and Governance bachelor. Its two 24-EC thesis tracks, Economics and Governance, are equally formal and neither is named by the target. The Economics track appears first in the current official structure and is selected neutrally, independently of UCR fit.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Economics, trade & quantitative analysis”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.
candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-2.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Public governance, institutions & policy”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.
candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-3.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Economics, politics, sociology, law, data and ethics foundations precede microeconomics, public economics, econometrics, EU politics, inequality and advanced policy analysis. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with nine 300-level courses.
